newsitem.title: GERMANY: German draft share law-credit institutes' holdings.
newsitem.headline: German draft share law-credit institutes' holdings.

text.p: The German Justice Ministry on Tuesday released details of a new draft share law. The following is a summary of the sections of the draft referring to credit institutions' share holdings.
The summary was provided by the ministry in German and translated by Reuters.

* Limitation on exercise of voting rights. Credit institutions may not exercise proxy votes in a shareholder meeting if they are also in the same meeting exercising votes from their own holding of more than five percent in the company. Shareholders continue to be allowed to hand over their proxy on a case by case basis. This regulation is intended to address the critical point of accumulation of the influence of credit institutes due to their own investment ownings and shareholder proxies.

* Increased transparency requirements for credit institutions in relation to the annual repoort. Credit institutions (whatever their legal form) must detail all mandates held by the members of their governing bodies and other staff and must also declare share holdings larger than five percent.
